report.scope: PBI-025 per docs/backlog/specs/pbi-025-local-tabs.md revision 3 (approved): the collector writes each project's five projectTabs records and its status record into the local SQLite database, with the git tab's pure half moved into the shared exporters/derive.py so the board and the local app derive one document from one implementation. Acceptance: T-1..T-6 from the PBI file plus AC-TB1..AC-TB14 from the spec. Grounding path: ran-suite (all three configured suites run from the worktree root).
report.summary: 6 files modified, 3 files created (local/tabs.py and two new local test modules); 45 tests added (11 in tests/, 34 in local/tests/); suites: python -m unittest discover -s tests 345 passed / 0 failed (baseline 334), node tests/page.test.mjs 99 passed / 0 failed (baseline 99), python -m unittest discover -s local/tests 303 passed / 0 failed (baseline 265). Nothing committed, staged, pushed or deployed; the change is in the working tree of C:/Users/jdk/dispatch-board-worktrees/PBI-025 only.

changes.why: The git tab's pure half moves into the shared module, per the parent spec's rule that all derivations live under exporters/ and the collector imports them: new git_default (the master/main/'' selection) and git_doc (the whole document from captured stdout, applying the ahead/shortstat emptiness rule itself so a caller cannot get the condition wrong), plus public_remote and its USERINFO pattern. No subprocess, no file read: derive's own contract is unchanged.

git_tab becomes a thin caller of derive.git_default and derive.git_doc, keeping its ten subprocess calls and their order; public_remote and USERINFO are re-exported through the existing `from derive import (...)` line, so no caller or test breaks. Output unchanged.

The tab and status pass: the OWNED constant (the five export_board suffixes, never records.TAB_NAMES), build() over each configured project with the per-project failure boundary, carry() for keep-last and carriedSince, owns()/project_of() for the two-writer scoping, and statuses() for refresh.py's live/updatedAt rule with the merge db.upsert cannot do itself.

Hooks the pass in: tabs.build before BEGIN IMMEDIATE (outside the write lock), tab and status added to the stored read, the stored tabs partitioned so a foreign suffix takes part in nothing, the carry rule applied inside the transaction, tab added to the deletion kinds, the guard's emptied-tabs clause added, and the status records written after the upserts and deletions from one clock reading shared with lastRefresh. Report gains tabs and statuses; summary gains ', N tabs'. run_pass gains data_dir and run.

Added a Git case class: git_doc over captured output (byDir, the commit split on the first pipe, tracked, dirty, redacted remotes), the emptiness rule exercised through git_doc's own signature, git_default's master-wins precedence, public_remote, and the assertion that derive still has no subprocess attribute. No existing case changed.

Added the in-run T-6 evidence: a verbatim pre-move _reference_git_tab driven through one shared fake git alongside the live git_tab over four input sets, compared on keys, values and key order; and byte-identity for the four deterministic spec tabs against a fixture captured from the pre-move code, with the test asserting none of the four holds the temporary root. No existing case changed.

The pass's own tests: building, carry, the network boundary, the shapes canary, the foreign-suffix protection, the status rule, deletion reasons, the guard observed from a second connection, per-project failure confinement and the per-record error.

The equivalence suite, built on test_conformance.Fixture consumed unmodified: tab documents equal after removing generatedAt and pulls, carriedSince equal on both sides, the findings document untouched by either writer, and refresh.plan's status documents agreeing with the collector's on live and on whether updatedAt moved.

Three assertions in the existing suite encoded the pre-PBI truth that the collector writes no tab or status record, which this change makes false by design: the Case tearDown's zero-rows check on statuses, the kinds set in test_only_the_five_kinds_are_written (renamed), and the summary line's regex. Each is re-expressed to the new behaviour; none is weakened or removed, and the answers-table and empty-project_tabs checks are kept.

follow_ups.reason: Three assertions of the PBI-019 suite were re-expressed because they encoded 'the collector writes no tab or status record', which this change makes false by design. The spec's §7 said 'new files only', which was a parallel-safety statement about PBI-026 (already merged at this PBI's base commit 5baa922); local/tests/** is in this work item's allowed areas and test_conformance.py, the file §7.4 protects, is untouched. Reviewer should confirm this reading.

run_pass gained two optional parameters the spec did not name, data_dir and run, so the tests can point the pass at a fixture's data folder and drive git without a repository; run mirrors export_board.main's existing run parameter. The command line passes neither, so its behaviour is the documented default.

A record that already carries carriedSince is returned unchanged in the intended set rather than omitted from it. Omitting it, as the row's 'store nothing' reads in isolation, put it in the deletion set and deleted it on the third pass; the unchanged-record check in _Pass.store still means db.upsert is not called, so both §4.4's 'db.upsert is not called' and §6.2's 'a tab goes only when its project leaves the config' hold. Caught by the carry-cycle test before it could reach the reviewer.

Where export_board.is_repo answers False when git cannot be run, the local one lets the OSError reach build's git handler, so a machine without git warns once per project per pass and carries the stored git tab, per §4.2.1 row 3. The documents are identical either way.

Two follow-up work items the spec recommends and this change does not cover: a config-sourced status block for title/message/metrics, and the local findings tab (which needs exporters/export_sessions.py, outside these areas). Q-2 carries an FYI to the owner that restoring pull requests locally would need a process outside the collector.
Both are in the work item's allowed areas and both are deliberately untouched: the spec settles on no cadence key and no gh key (Q-5, Q-13). An unused allowed area is not a defect.
No copy of the schema module was found on this machine, so this report was written to the documented shape by hand and its validate() was NOT run.
